transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Any time I’m near where there might be snakes, I feel an immediate rush of fear that I can’t shake. It's gotten to the point where it's starting to affect my work and my personal life, so a colleague suggested I come speak with someone.
Do you go out of your way to avoid places or activities where you might encounter snakes, even when the actual danger is low? How much is this fear interfering with your work or daily life?

Yes, I go completely out of my way to avoid them, like delegating school nature walks to other staff and even rewriting a grant proposal to cut out outdoor activities that might involve reptiles. It has also spilled into my personal life, forcing me to skip hikes with my club, which leaves me feeling embarrassed and like I’m not doing my job fully.
When you react this way, do you recognize that your fear of snakes is stronger than the actual danger in most situations? Or does it feel completely justified to you?

Yes, I absolutely recognize that my fear is way out of proportion to any actual danger. Logically, I know a small snake can't really do much to hurt me, but in the moment, the fear is so overwhelming and out of control that my brain just panics anyway.
How long have you had this intense fear of snakes and the avoidance that comes with it? Has it been present for at least 6 months?

Yes, it has been going on for much longer than six months. It actually started a little over two years ago after a planning visit to a reptile exhibit, and it has only gotten more entrenched since then.
